refuted_claims: A task's STDOUT is invisible in every operator-visible surface — REFUTED 3/3: `forjar logs --resource` does print it; true claim is narrower (every APPLY-TIME surface).
The reporter's cached-transcript theory — REFUTED by append-only counter files proving the command re-ran on every apply.
29.2s is too fast to be a real build — REFUTED: a warm cmake reconfigure measured 0.67s on this machine; 4 of the 5 'failed' were dependents that executed nothing.
-v/-vv/-vvv would have surfaced the stdout — REFUTED: all three are byte-identical; they echo the SCRIPT SOURCE, never runtime stdout.
The on-disk run log made the output discoverable — REFUTED: only `forjar logs --resource` prints it, the failure names no path, and --state-dir defaults to a relative dir a CI runner deletes.
#391 (completion_check hashing) fixed the reported symptom — REFUTED: the reporter ran the patched binary and saw the identical failure.
The exit-1 came from the command failing — REFUTED: the command exited 0; the GH-254 completion_check re-assertion exited 1.
The final process error carries a diagnostic — REFUTED: it carries only a count.
Renaming the resource would clear stuck state — REFUTED: a brand-new resource id failed identically.
A skipped dependent is distinguishable from a real failure in machine-readable output — REFUTED: it folds into resources_failed with error: null.
The `.script` sidecar records what actually executed — REFUTED: it records the PRE-wrap script, before the stdin-isolation wrapper.
`--timeout` bounds an SSH task — REFUTED: measured 48s wall for --timeout 3; the ControlMaster holds the killed child's pipe.
Per-resource durations reconcile against the machine total — REFUTED: sampled before post-apply verification.
forjar's failure string is bounded — REFUTED: out.stderr.trim() was unbounded into an append-only event log.
The parallel path behaves like the sequential one — REFUTED: it writes no run log and skips post-apply verification entirely.
`--log-file` offers a file-based escape hatch — REFUTED: it is listed as inert in src/cli/inert_flags.rs.
`continue_independent` still surfaces the failure on the console — REFUTED: the only print site is gated on StopOnFirst.
quorum.divergence: lanes disagreed before synthesis: replay-cache and timing-summary initially attributed the symptom to different mechanisms (state poisoning vs. build timing); both converged on stream routing only after the live-repro lane's counter-file evidence. 17 of 60 claims were killed.

systems: Ansible — every module result carries stdout/stderr/rc as SEPARATE fields; the operator never has to guess which stream a diagnostic went to
Kubernetes — `kubectl describe pod` surfaces both streams plus the last-terminated state on CrashLoopBackOff; `kubectl logs` is a first-class verb, not a buried path
Terraform — remote-exec provisioner streams BOTH stdout and stderr to the operator live, prefixed per-resource, rather than collecting stderr at exit
GNU make — prints the failing recipe line verbatim with its output, so the operator sees what ran, not only that it failed
crux.verdict: forjar was BELOW the field default, not making a design trade-off. Every surveyed system surfaces both streams or makes the transcript a first-class verb; forjar printed stderr only and named no path to the rest. The fix moves it to parity, and the head+tail excerpt (keeping the pre-build lines) is slightly ahead of Terraform's tail-biased streaming for this failure shape.
